messages:
sara: Thinking aloud — should SDKs surface any rollout/pin metadata to user code? would be handy for debugging behavior differences.
tom: I like visibility but worried about leaking internal experiment names or tenant identifiers.
vijay: Agreed on leak risk. We should define a vetted public view that strips PII and freeform labels.
eli: Runtime note: including extra JSON in responses adds tokens and can affect latency for short prompts. headers vs body?
yuki: headers are lower footprint but CORS + browser clients complicate. Perhaps make it opt-in per route, default header for server-to-server.
sara: Proposed minimal public schema: model_label, channel(=stable/canary), soft_expiry, opaque_ref. opaque_ref should be HMAC'd so ops can map back but external users can't.
tom: HMAC with per-tenant salt + rotation. store mapping table internally. do not include tenant id or raw rollout id.
vijay: Also: SDKs should ignore unknown fields (forward-compat). add a metadata_version integer to aid parsing.
eli: Telemetry pipeline: separate telemetry-only tags that never go to client SDKs. sampling guidance required to avoid cardinality explosion.
yuki: Policy: default SDK exposure ON for self-serve orgs, OFF for enterprise by account flag. mention in privacy docs.
ops-bot: heads-up: staging experiment flag rollout-metadata-public enabled for 5% traffic.
sara: Action items: 1) write short RFC follow-up with schema + threat model; 2) HMAC plan and rotation; 3) SDK parsing rules and minor version; 4) telemetry sampling and retention.
tom: I'll own HMAC rotation doc. vijay can do telemetry sampling guidance. eli will prototype header vs body config.
vijay: Quick add: avoid freeform strings as enums where possible. allow a short description field that's opt-in and audited.
sara: Great. I'll draft RFC and include example mapping queries from opaque_ref -> deployment record. will include migration strategy for older clients.
ops-bot: created task RED-8123 to track RFC + infra work.
yuki: Thanks — ping when RFC is ready for review. :thumbsup:
